- [把 eBPF 安全代理的内核 CPU 开销砍掉 90%：靠的是记忆化，不是 AI](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-14_ebpf-memoization-90-percent/): Translation+analysis of nathan naveen's blog (2026-09-11). An eBPF file-open LSM security agent caches per-inode policy decisions in a `BPF_MAP_TYPE_LRU_HASH` (max_entries 10000); key = mntns_id + mount_id + inode (inode numbers only unique per mount tree, mntns prevents cross-namespace reuse), value = access_index (bitmask) + state. Benchmark: same file opened 200,000 times, kernel cycles dropped from 28B to 3.03B (~90%); `is_restricted_filepath`/`path_check_callback` fell to ~0.02% of stack (perf cycles:k). Edge case: hardlinks share an inode, so when `i_nlink != 1` the cache is skipped and it falls back to the slow path — correctness over hit rate. Repo: bomfather/agent.
  - Key topics: eBPF, LSM, memoization, BPF_MAP_TYPE_LRU_HASH, inode cache, hardlink, i_nlink, performance, dentry, mount namespace

- [rspamd 把 46% 的合法邮件丢进了垃圾箱：一次从配置文件体系开始的排查](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-23_rspamd-false-positive-tuning/): Hands-on false-positive audit of a self-hosted mail gateway (Debian 12 + postfix + dovecot + rspamd 4.2.0), with a systematic walkthrough of rspamd's five-layer configuration system (`rspamd.conf` top-level orchestration; `local.d/` per-key merge vs `override.d/` whole-section strict override; `scores.d/` + `groups.conf` symbol weights; `actions.conf` score thresholds; `modules.d/`, `settings.conf`, `rspamd.local.lua`, `maps.d/` as extension points). Measured outcome: legitimate mail misfiled to Junk dropped from 294/643 (46%) to 40/643 (6%), and per-message scan time from ~4136 ms to 611-1236 ms. Five stacked root causes: (1) `/etc/rspamd/options.inc` had been truncated to 25 lines from the packaged 93 (`options.inc.dpkg-dist`), dropping `filters = "chartable,dkim,regexp,fuzzy_check"`. rspamd's own docs state C modules are enabled only via the `filters` attribute and "if no filters attribute is defined, all C modules are disabled"; these are statically linked into `librspamd-server.so` (`nm -D | grep -ci dkim` = 31, `src/plugins/dkim_check.c` present) with no `.lua` file on disk, so nothing is visible in a file listing. Consequence: `R_DKIM_ALLOW`/`NA`/`REJECT` never registered, silently disabling `WHITELIST_DKIM`, `WHITELIST_SPF_DKIM`, `WHITELIST_DMARC`, `TRUSTED_NEWSLETTER_PASS`, `DMARC_CHECK` and `NO_AUTH_SPOOF` — while `configtest` still printed `syntax OK` with only `destination ... is missing` warnings. The same stub also dropped `dns{timeout=1s;sockets=16;retransmits=5}` and `local_addrs`; rspamd.log showed 1304 `query timed out` per day (concentrated on `asn6.rspamd.com` and DNSWL/URIBL zones), suppressing negative signals such as `DWL_DNSWL_HI` (-3.5). (2) `override.d/policies_group.conf` is priority=10 strict override, and its 28-line version omitted all six `R_DKIM_*` weights, yielding `R_DKIM_ALLOW has no score registered` — a case where `local.d/` (per-key merge) was the correct tool and `override.d/` was not. (3) `FORGED_SENDER` (+5.0) fires whenever envelope `MAIL FROM` and header `From` are not the same mailbox (`same_mailbox()` in `forged_recipients.lua`), which is exactly how every ESP works by design: `publishing@email.mckinsey.com` / `bounce@email.mckinsey.com`, `jobs-noreply@linkedin.com` / `m-1but2tww...@bounce.linkedin.com`, `notifications@github.com` / `bounces@sgmail.github.com`, and VERP mailing lists `author@debian.org` / `bounce-debian-list=user=freelamp.com@lists.debian.org`. In a 3687-message archive, 1785 messages had an envelope domain different-but-related to the header domain and every one was legitimate, zero spam; rspamd's built-in `ENVFROM_PRVS` only matches `prvs=`, `btv1==`, `msprvs1=` and had 0 hits in production. Fixed by a custom Lua symbol `RELAY_ENVELOPE` (score -5.0): envelope domain organisationally related to the header domain AND envelope shaped like a relay AND at least one of SPF/DKIM/DMARC passing; offline coverage of legitimate mail reached 98.5% (2426/2463). The authentication condition is load-bearing — without it a genuine unauthenticated spoof whose domains happen to be related would be waved through. (4) A `force_actions` rule named `BLOCK_SPOOFED_LOCAL_DOMAIN` used the expression `FORGED_SENDER & !DMARC_POLICY_ALLOW & !R_SPF_ALLOW` — which contains no local-domain test at all — so it hard-rejected any message whose envelope differed from its From and lacked SPF/DMARC; production showed 32 forced rejects, 22 of them legitimate `lists.debian.org` posts where `freelamp.com` was merely a VERP tag. Replaced by a Lua symbol `SPOOFED_LOCAL_DOMAIN` that genuinely checks the header From domain against `LOCAL_DOMAINS` and requires SPF, DKIM and DMARC all to have failed plus a non-authenticated, non-local origin. Note: `force_actions.lua` ignores an `enable` key (its rules loop reads only `sett.action` and `sett.expression`), verified by configtest, so the block must be commented out rather than disabled. (5) A global Dovecot Sieve script gated Junk filing on `X-Spam: Yes`, but that header is generated by `milter_headers.lua`'s `x-spam-status` routine under the condition `action ~= 'no action' and action ~= 'greylist'`, making its real threshold `add_header = 6` in `actions.conf`, not `reject = 15` — collapsing the entire 6-to-15 band into a binary verdict. Rewritten to test `X-Rspamd-Action` for `reject`/`rewrite subject` or `X-Spamd-Bar` with eight `+` (one per point). Regression methodology and three traps: `dovecot-keywords` is a per-mailbox index map (the same letter means `NonJunk` in INBOX but something else in another folder, so cross-applying one map inverts the labels and flips the conclusion); re-scanning Maildir breaks DKIM body hashes because stored messages use LF rather than the original CRLF, making `R_DKIM_REJECT` an artifact — judge real DKIM verdicts from `rspamd.log` instead; and rspamd re-reads the `X-Spam: Yes` header it wrote on the previous pass, triggering `SPAM_FLAG` for a spurious +5.0, so self-generated headers must be stripped before any rescan. Bottom line: a passing `configtest` does not mean the checks are running — verify with `rspamc counters` that the symbols actually exist.
  - Key topics: rspamd, postfix, dovecot, spam filtering, false positives, mail gateway, DKIM, SPF, DMARC, Sieve, FORGED_SENDER, ESP bounce address, VERP, local.d vs override.d, actions.conf thresholds, rspamd.local.lua, configtest, Debian 12
  - Diagnostic commands: `rspamadm configtest`, `rspamc counters | grep R_DKIM`, `rspamc stat`, `diff /etc/rspamd/options.inc /etc/rspamd/options.inc.dpkg-dist`, `nm -D /usr/lib/rspamd/librspamd-server.so | grep -ci dkim`, `wc -l /etc/rspamd/{scores.d,override.d}/policies_group.conf`, `journalctl -u opendkim -u rspamd`, `sieve-test <script> <message.eml`, `doveadm fetch`, `cat /path/dovecot-keywords`

### 开源/工具

- [从「能免费在车里唱歌」出发，我为什么会撞上三种歌词格式](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-18_lrc-ttml-karaoke-formats/): A field report that starts from three non-negotiable requirements -- own local files, free, and usable in the car -- and follows each one into a different layer of the lyric-format mess. Establishes up front that CarPlay and Android Auto are mutually exclusive (CarPlay is Apple's proprietary interface, Android Auto is Google's; neither can be implemented by an app on the other platform), that which one a car supports is a hardware property software cannot supply, and that an Android phone on a CarPlay-only head unit falls back to Bluetooth with no head-unit library browsing. Records two first-hand iOS disappointments: OnePlayer, whose free tier cannot even skip tracks, with an in-app purchase list that also sells monthly and yearly Pro plus per-minute AI lyric recognition; and play:Sub, a mature Subsonic/Navidrome client whose offline mode is cache-semantic, meaning your away-from-home library is whatever you synced while on Wi-Fi, and whose official description states a licensed Subsonic server installation is required -- so a complete library on the road either means manual pre-caching or exposing the backend port to the internet. Concludes the four-way filter (free, fully offline, word-level lyrics, car head unit) leaves only Gramophone on Android and Steve on iOS, confirmed by implementation rather than marketing: Gramophone implements MediaLibraryService and registers automotiveApp metadata, Steve's description states word-by-word highlighting comes from TTML. Then the format history: LRC introduced in 1998 by Taiwan-based Kuo (Djohan) Shiang-shiang's Lyrics Displayer with a Winamp plug-in, described by Wikipedia as one of the first programs to simulate karaoke, and never formally defined by any standards body -- quoting AMLL's documentation that its original source is unknown and it became an industry convention with many variants and unspecified details; the A2 extension added by the author of A2 Media Player replacing square brackets with angle brackets; and TTML, which began in 2003 as DFXP, became TTML1 in November 2010 and TTML2 in November 2018, and earned Netflix HBO Telestream SMPTE and W3C an Emmy in 2015 for non-live broadband captioning standardisation, which is why its design goals are broadcast subtitles rather than sing-along, with a dedicated W3C TTML Karaoke Extension Module draft existing precisely because expressing karaoke in TTML needs extra specification. Presents eight word-level dialects with an ownership column as the point: LRC (nobody), LRC A2 (a player author), SPL (one app's author, standards document dated 16 December 2024 and signed by the Salt Player developer, which also cannot directly accept standard A2 because it requires an explicit line-end timestamp), YRC (NetEase), QRC (QQ Music, TripleDES then zlib/inflate), KRC (Kugou, XOR then zlib), Lyricify Syllable, and TTML (W3C) -- only one is an international standard. Names the reason the commercial ones are encrypted: word timings are content assets, so encryption blocks bulk scraping and competitor reuse, and no platform has ever published its spec, leaving open-source readers to reverse-engineer with code comments citing ported decrypt routines. Then the deeper layer, lyric database openness: LRCLIB is the only genuinely open one (free, no API key, CORS enabled, MIT server code, periodic public SQLite dumps, and the author's own Hacker News line about zero profit intention), and its API's hasWordSync field shows the format supports word timings while most records are line-level because contributors upload line-level LRC -- which is why word timings must be generated rather than fetched; Spotify has no lyrics endpoint in its Web API at all, licences them from Musixmatch, returns LINE_SYNCED with the word field empty, and the only developer route is scraping an account-bound cookie that expires; Musixmatch is legally cleanest and most expensive, with Sony Universal Warner licences, roughly 30 and 120 dollars monthly tiers, word-level timing only on the higher tier, and an explicit prohibition on caching or storing lyrics on both self-serve plans, which conflicts directly with offline playback, while the App Store's rule requiring proof of lyric rights is exactly what its licence confirmation letter satisfies. Closes the loop on why free word-level players are scarce, documents the three conversion failures on real files -- fixed-width Chinese segmentation producing cuts inside words and needing Charabia, Booming appending a space after every non-final word in LrcLyricsParser so Chinese always renders as 雨 一直 下, and Steve's LRC reader being line-level only and not stripping angle-bracket tags so enhanced LRC shows timestamps as lyric text, plus backing up already-converted files by mistake -- and states the working arrangement as one original LRC generating both enhanced LRC and TTML. Explicitly names the limitation of the character-proportional timing used here (an estimate that drifts on held notes and fast runs) and contrasts it with forced alignment via Whisper and wav2vec2 reaching millisecond precision at the cost of GPU time and model downloads, framing character-proportional timing as sufficient-but-drifting versus alignment as accurate-but-expensive.
  - Key topics: LRC, LRC A2, Enhanced LRC, A2 Media Player, Lyrics Displayer, Winamp, Kuo Shiang-shiang, TTML, TTML1, TTML2, DFXP, W3C Timed Text Working Group, TTML Karaoke Extension Module, IMSC, SMPTE, FCC safe harbour, WebVTT, AMLL, SPL, Salt Player, 椒盐音乐, NetEase YRC, QQ Music QRC, Kugou KRC, TripleDES, zlib, XOR, reverse engineering, word-by-word lyrics, syllable timing, hasWordSync, LRCLIB, MIT, SQLite dump, Hacker News, Musixmatch, Sony, Universal, Warner, LINE_SYNCED, no-caching clause, App Store licence certification, Gramophone, 留声机, Steve, Booming, Local Player, NeoMusic, Fluxio, OnePlayer, play:Sub, Subsonic, Navidrome, CarPlay, Android Auto, F-Droid, GPLv3, Charabia, Chinese word segmentation, CJK spacing, itunes:timing, LrcLyricsParser, text rebuild verification, forced alignment, Whisper, wav2vec2, WhisperX

- [GNOME 这个 AI 聊天应用最值得看的不是功能，而是它把「哪些数据会出去」写成了可核对的句子](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-17_moose-0-6-gnome-ai-chat-privacy/): Translation+analysis of Phoronix's brief on Moose 0.6 and 0.6.1 together with the project's README and release history, treating the privacy design as the story rather than the feature list. Establishes what Moose is: a GNOME-aligned AI chat application built on GTK4 and libadwaita, written in Rust under GPL-3.0-or-later, distributed via Flathub, created 11 May 2026 and having reached 34 stars and one fork by 17 October 2026, with releases v0.4.3 in June, v0.5.0 in September, v0.6.0 on 7 October and v0.6.1 on 17 October. Covers the 0.6 additions (secure cloud connections with protected credential storage, a Local-Only mode using Ollama managed by Moose, permission handling settable per chat or remembered across chats of the same provider, a GNOME Files browser for attaching files to conversations, and an expanded local model catalogue for chat vision reasoning and coding) and the 0.6.1 follow-on adding Mistral and DeepSeek, plus the full connection list including Ollama managed by Moose, an existing Ollama instance, Ollama Cloud, Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini and later Mistral and DeepSeek. Then extracts three design decisions Phoronix's summary flattens into a feature list: that API keys go to the desktop keyring rather than an application-managed store, with the argument that this matters because the app holds keys for many providers so centralising them keeps the keys visible to the user and auditable at the system level, and pairing it with the README line that cloud and external Ollama requests send the approved conversation context to the selected provider where approved signals an authorised rather than default action; that Local-Only mode and the per-request permission prompt are two different switches, one a global intention blocking remote inference and the other a per-chat or per-provider authorisation remembered across chats, with the argument that a single switch would force users to choose between the inconvenience of never using cloud and the inconvenience of confirming every time, and the generalisation that intention and authorisation are long-term policy versus specific action and that conflating them is why many privacy settings fail; and that the README writes the data flows as three checkable sentences separating conversations and the document library stored on your computer, local inference through the Moose-managed Ollama, and cloud or external Ollama requests sending approved conversation context to the chosen provider, which lets readers draw their own conclusion rather than trust an adjective. Notes the README's honest limits that images need a vision-capable model and that PDFs need selectable text since scanned pages are not read automatically, consistent with the build dependency on Poppler's pdftotext, and observes that the tag list emphasises local-ai offline-ai and ollama while chatgpt-alternative names what it wants to replace. Argues the ordering matters, since an application whose default path is local must have cloud explicitly added and asks for confirmation at each step whereas a cloud-first application organises its permission design around making cloud frictionless, and connects this to earlier coverage of a EUR 25 one-off local document tool and a 28-service self-hosting writeup where local is the default and network is the explicit exception, noting that this ordering determines the consequence of forgetting to configure something. States the material's limits honestly, that Phoronix is a brief with no user numbers, no independent audit of actual privacy behaviour and limited maintainer information, so the article is framed as a design writeup worth learning from rather than a recommendation to use it. Closes by placing Moose on the other side of the AI-material spectrum from the AI-contribution policies recently covered, where those ask what code may enter a project and Moose asks what data may leave a machine, and that its right move is to write the boundary as checkable sentences rather than argue for trust.
  - Key topics: Moose, GNOME, GTK4, libadwaita, Rust, GPL-3.0-or-later, Flathub, Flatpak, Ollama, Ollama Cloud, Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, local AI, offline AI, Local-Only mode, remote inference, permission per chat, per-provider permission, credential storage, desktop keyring, Secret Service, GNOME Keyring, KWallet, API keys, approved conversation context, document library, FTS5, SQLite, GtkSourceView, Poppler, pdftotext, vision model, scanned PDF, chatgpt-alternative, privacy design, data flows, 译文


- [Starling 又用 Claude 写出了一个办公套件：而它和同一周那批 AI 政策，正好指向相反的方向](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-16_starling-office-ai-generated-suite/): Translation+analysis of Phoronix's report on Starling Office v0.1 (16 October 2026) together with the project's own documentation and its July debut coverage, framed around the contrast with the five open source AI contribution policies covered this same week. Establishes what Starling is: a Linux desktop environment where the shell, compositor, framework and first-party apps are Swift, with a full port of Flutter's Dart framework to Swift and no Dart VM, running on the Flutter engine's C core through a DRM/KMS embedder and a sibling engine repository, with its own code under Apache-2.0 while the framework port and engine retain upstream licences. Explains the deliberate split in the stack, with the Wayland compositor kept as roughly 5,700 lines of C because the protocol ecosystem already lives there and everything above it in Swift, the in-tree X11 server with DRI3/Present so X11 clients run, and the protocols implemented (xdg-shell, linux-dmabuf zero-copy import, viewporter, fractional-scale-v1, pointer-constraints, relative-pointer, text-input-v3, presentation-time, primary-selection, idle-inhibit, cursor-shape-v1, xdg-decoration, xdg-activation, xdg-output, wlr-data-control). Preserves the project's own reasoning for building a desktop on a GUI framework, that a desktop environment and a modern GUI framework already do almost the same work so tiling, spaces, Mission Control and the glass work on real applications for free, and acknowledges that the remaining half is enormous, a Wayland server, an X11 server, window management, multi-monitor hot-plug, portals and a set of applications, which has always been team work measured in decades, noting the project's line that the idea was never the expensive part and that there are a handful of Linux desktops rather than hundreds not because nobody had an idea. Then quotes the most candid statement about AI's role: that AI is what closed the gap, not curiosity or architecture, that the question, the bet on building a desktop as a GUI framework and every judgement about what Starling should be were the author's, and that what AI made possible was carrying it out, writing the hundreds of thousands of lines between an idea and a desktop you can log into fast enough that one person could stay ahead of it and keep steering, with the line that a curious person with a bold idea is not new but being able to act on it alone is. Highlights three technical points worth attention beyond the AI label: the unprivileged session where DRM master and input come from logind via libseat rather than running as root, which matters more than usual in a project with large amounts of AI-generated code because it bounds what compromise yields; the verified real applications (Chrome, VS Code, Slack, IntelliJ, GIMP and Blender with its EEVEE viewport via linux-dmabuf) covering Chromium/Electron, Qt6, GTK3/4, the JetBrains Runtime and Blender's GHOST, which shows the compositor can display programs written by strangers; and the distinction the project draws between a port and a wrapper, where the Swift compiler embedding Clang lets engine headers import through a module map with no FFI layer, generated bindings or shim. Records the honest limits at different points in time, that the July v0.2 preview was tested on AMD and virtio-gpu but not Intel or NVIDIA, had scaling pinned at 2.0 and was Ubuntu 26.04 only, and that by a September v0.4.0 summary there was no screen lock, an incomplete portal and a README stating interfaces change without notice, explicitly not for anyone needing a daily driver, plus that the project is maintained by one anonymous developer which raises sustainability questions. Covers Starling Office v0.1 itself: a word processor, spreadsheet and presentation editor handling DOCX XLSX PPTX, written in Swift and again with Claude Code, not dependent on the Starling desktop, offered as Flatpak and Debian packages for Linux plus macOS and Windows binaries and triable in the browser, with Phoronix's author reporting it worked in a brief Ubuntu test, while noting that supporting OOXML and being compatible with Word Excel and PowerPoint are different claims and that a v0.1 that opens files is far from identical layout. Argues the contrast with GCC the Linux kernel Debian Flathub and Libreboot is not about who is right but about two different problems, presenting a table across project age, scarcest resource, the main risk AI introduces, the main benefit and who bears long-term maintenance, and concluding that a project's tolerance for AI depends more on its history than its values since a twenty-year-old C codebase must have someone understand and answer for generated patches for twenty more years while a project created in July has no compatibility burden or protected historical decisions. Closes by arguing AI lowered the cost of creation without lowering the cost of commitment, that Starling's own stress on staying ahead and steering matches the broader pattern where generation gets cheap and judgement becomes the bottleneck, that the risk here is the single-maintainer structure rather than the AI authorship, that expectations for the office suite should be legibility and modifiability rather than replacing LibreOffice, and that the two positions sit on different time scales so a project that completes its lifecycle will eventually move from the former to the latter.
  - Key topics: Starling, Starling Office, Starling SDK, Swift, Flutter, Dart VM, starling-engine, flutter-swift, Wayland compositor, X11 server, DRI3, Present, DRM/KMS embedder, libseat, logind, unprivileged session, GDM, xdg-shell, linux-dmabuf, viewporter, fractional-scale-v1, pointer-constraints, text-input-v3, presentation-time, primary-selection, idle-inhibit, cursor-shape-v1, xdg-decoration, xdg-activation, xdg-output, wlr-data-control, Chrome, VS Code, Slack, IntelliJ, GIMP, Blender, EEVEE, GHOST, Qt6, GTK3, GTK4, JetBrains Runtime, Electron, Chromium, Apache-2.0, Ubuntu 26.04, Flatpak, Debian, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, OOXML, LibreOffice, ONLYOFFICE, Claude Code, AI-generated code, open source governance, single maintainer, sustainability, GCC, Linux kernel, Debian, Flathub, Libreboot, AGENTS.md


- [Timescale 把向量索引做进了 PostgreSQL 的 C 内核里：一次索引重建换来的 10 倍，值不值](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-16_pg-vectorsearch-prism-index-timescale/): Translation+analysis of the pg_vectorsearch repository and its documentation, noting the repository metrics measured on 16 October 2026 (363 stars, 13 forks, created 30 January 2026, primarily C, PostgreSQL licence) and the project's own alpha status warning that upgrading between prereleases may not be possible and that users should plan to drop and recreate the extension and its indexes. Leads with the two things that matter most: that a PRISM index can be built directly on existing pgvector vector or halfvec columns without rewriting or copying the column, which makes migration a cost question rather than a performance question, and the three limits the README states rather than hides. Covers the four advertised features (PRISM as an IVF-style index with hierarchical routing aimed above 100 million vectors, RaBitQ quantisation with theoretical error bounds for two-stage search, SIMD distance computation across AVX2, AVX512 and NEON, and dynamic updates with posting-list splits via prism_rebalance), the performance claim of being faster at equivalent recall than pgvector's HNSW on a 100-million-vector dataset with a quarter of the memory, and the placement of PRISM conceptually alongside IVFFlat but built around modern quantisation, routing and partitioning in C. Reproduces the five-step query flow and singles out the error-bound mechanism as the reason memory can be saved while recall holds: since a quantised encoding carries a bound rather than only an estimate, the search can safely exclude candidates that cannot possibly be nearest neighbours instead of merely ranking them, so full-precision reranking from the heap touches far fewer vectors, which is also the cost structure of the design. Explains the compatibility design where vec32 and vec16 are binary-compatible with pgvector's vector and halfvec but differently named so both extensions coexist even in one schema, and the recommended migration path of building PRISM alongside HNSW, verifying with EXPLAIN that the planner prefers it, then dropping HNSW, which turns an index swap into a rollback-able and observable process; includes the operator class mapping table and the mechanical rename rule for replacing HNSW indexes. Covers the three stated limits and their consequences: alpha status meaning index rebuilds on upgrade, posting lists that never split on their own so prism_rebalance or REINDEX is needed because inserts only append, and the STORAGE PLAIN note explaining that the default EXTERNAL toasts values over about 2 kB and rerank then pays an extra fetch the planner does not cost, a caveat found in a SQL comment rather than a documentation page. Closes by arguing the real adoption driver is that neither the table nor the queries must change, that the error-bound approach generalises to any system trading approximation for speed because the useful question is not how accurate the approximation is but whether you can know where it is inaccurate, and that the README's honesty about limits is what makes the current suitability (test rather than production) legible while the missing recall-latency curves, build times, absolute memory and benchmark configuration leave the performance claim to be reproduced on the reader's own data.
  - Key topics: PostgreSQL, pgvector, vector search, ANN, approximate nearest neighbour, PRISM, Partitioned Routing Index for Similarity Matching, IVF, IVFFlat, HNSW, hierarchical routing, centroid tree, posting list, RaBitQ, quantisation, error bound, two-stage search, reranking, SIMD, AVX2, AVX512, NEON, vec32, vec16, halfvec, operator classes, l2_ops, ip_ops, cosine_ops, prism.nprobe, prism_rebalance, REINDEX, TOAST, STORAGE PLAIN, EXTERNAL, Meon build, CBLAS, PostgreSQL 18, Timescale, TigerData, SPFresh, SPANN, SIGMOD 2024, SOSP 2023, NeurIPS 2021, alpha, 译文

Then covers the technical change: EDK2 becomes the default payload with GRUB and SeaBIOS provided in flash as EFI builds for backward compatibility, marked by a bold warning that major design changes may affect existing setups; explains why this matters given that EDK2 is Intel's BSD-licensed reference implementation of UEFI even though vendor forks are proprietary, and that Libreboot goes from providing almost no UEFI beyond U-Boot on a few boards to providing full UEFI with all four freedoms intact on nearly every supported board, with the tested operating system list including Windows 10 and 11, 9front, Linux UKI bootloaders and systemd-boot (so modern distro installs no longer require GRUB), OpenBSD with an EFI bootloader and GPT partitioning (older SeaBIOS txtmode could only do MBR), and FreeBSD in UEFI mode, with ReactOS failing for lack of UEFI support. Preserves the caveats including that 32-bit-only boards still use bare GRUB/SeaBIOS against the announcement's own boast of all boards, that rebar stays disabled by default because enabling it breaks Intel GPU output under libgfxinit, that the Fam15h EDK2 images are source-only because the AST2050 needs a framebuffer, and that bare-metal payloads are now deprecated and may be removed. Argues the payload swap removed the real constraint on hardware support by moving from per-OS adaptation to an existing consensus, praises the treat-upstream-as-upstream stance and the diff-based sync method, contrasts this path with GNU Boot on the same KGPE-D16 hardware where the constraint is no nonfree code and therefore the improvements available differ, and notes the build-time MAC randomisation as a design that satisfies both developer convenience and release reproducibility by separating them with a condition rather than compromising either.

- [GNU Boot 加入 FSF 财政赞助：这一步解决的是「谁替你收钱」，但没解决「我的笔记本能不能用」](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-15_gnu-boot-fsf-fiscal-sponsorship/): Translation+analysis of the FSF's announcement on 14 September 2026 that GNU Boot became its latest fiscally sponsored project, correcting two common misreadings. Explains what GNU Boot is and is not: a 100% free software project aimed at replacing nonfree boot software like BIOS or UEFI, but explicitly only a distribution reusing existing projects such as Coreboot GRUB and SeaBIOS, with three tasks of finding and removing nonfree software in reused projects, building and assembling something installable with testing and installation and upgrade instructions, and providing good default configuration. Details the fiscal sponsorship mechanism (for projects conferences and groups that want to avoid becoming a formally incorporated entity, with expenditures vetted by the FSF but directed by the project's appointed representative in return for a 10% administrative fee) and its four benefit categories: funding capability including many donation forms plus workplace giving and corporate matching with the FSF handling acknowledgement documentation and regulatory requirements, fundraising support, decades of technical legal and nonprofit management experience plus licensing guidance from the FSF's Licensing and Compliance Lab, and office infrastructure. Corrects the misconception that GNU Boot replaces modern computers' proprietary BIOS or UEFI by examining the official status page for 0.1 RC6, showing that tested hardware is largely 2006 to 2009 era machines such as the ThinkPad X60 X200 T400s and X301 and the Asus KGPE-D16, that most cells read untested or missing images rather than unsupported, and that there is at least one explicit failure (Gigabyte D945GCLF2D under SeaBIOS text mode, bug 66463) with the official definition of failure requiring confirmation that it is a software rather than hardware problem. Explains the physical rather than software reason for the narrow hardware range, since modern x86 boot paths contain firmware components running on internal microcontrollers that cannot be replaced by free software. Covers the project's origin as a genuinely libre Libreboot, founded in 2022 by Denis GNUtoo Carikli and Adrien neox Bourmault, with the full timeline (Libreboot first released December 2013, briefly a GNU project April to September 2016, withdrawn from GNU in January 2017 after a months-long dispute, beginning to include non-libre code in November 2022 under its binary blob reduction policy), the parallel that Libreboot joined SPI as an associated project on 8 September 2025 while GNU Boot joined the FSF a year later, and the core argument preserved from GNU Boot's own page that a program should be called free or libre only when it is free in its entirety because mislabelling tends to lead the community astray. Highlights the under-noticed technical strength: the 0.1 RC6 build was made on Trisquel Aramo 11.0.1 in a virtual machine running on a KGPE-D16 that itself runs GNU Boot and is hosted by the French nonprofit Libre en communs, forming a closed trust chain, and that the gnuboot-trisquel-grub.img used for automated testing is reproducible and offered as an example for making other Guix-built components reproducible, explaining why reproducibility is decisive for boot firmware as the machine's root of trust. Closes by arguing the news is about administrative infrastructure rather than technical progress, that both limitations are hardware and process facts rather than signs of neglect, that the naming argument generalises as a point about terminology accuracy being a public good, and that the project's value is best understood as an existence proof that the span from power-on to OS handover can be completed with fully auditable reproducible free code.
  - Key topics: GNU Boot, FSF fiscal sponsorship, Working Together for Free Software Fund, 10% administrative fee, incorporation, Libreboot, coreboot, GRUB, SeaBIOS, U-Boot, binary blob reduction policy, Denis GNUtoo Carikli, Adrien neox Bourmault, Trisquel, Guix, reproducibility, reproducible builds, gnuboot-trisquel-grub.img, KGPE-D16, Libre en communs, ThinkPad X60, X200, T400s, X301, D945GCLF2D, 0.1 RC6, hardware support matrix, untested, missing images, Intel ME, AMD PSP, SPI Software in the Public Interest, naming and terminology accuracy, 译文

- [F-Droid 2.0 发布：十年最大改版，重写为 Kotlin Compose，安装体验终于追上系统商店](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-24_fdroid-2-0-release/): Translation+analysis of F-Droid's official blog (2026-09-24). F-Droid 2.0 is a complete redesign of the official Android app — the **largest update in 10 years**, after 14 test releases, rolling out over the coming weeks. Navigation is simplified into **Discover / Search / My Apps**; categories are greatly expanded and refined (VPNs, firewalls, password managers, launchers, navigation; the **Games** category reworked into **17 genres**) with higher-level "meta" categories; **search** now covers descriptions, categories and translated content (major improvements for **CJK/Chinese-Japanese-Korean** users, remembers recent queries); multi-criteria **filtering** (category, device compatibility, anti-features — e.g. device-compatible Action games excluding apps that depend on non-free network services) plus onboarding. **Install experience**: thanks largely to the EU's **Digital Markets Act (DMA)** and antitrust pressure, Android now offers all stores a smoother path; F-Droid 2.0 uses a **unified installer** and the new **pre-approval API** so users confirm right after deciding to install (not after download), bringing it close to the built-in store. Changes/removals: **updates fetch and install by default** (the **best refresh button is the one you never press**); pull-to-refresh is now scroll-only (manual trigger moved to the My Apps overflow menu); reworked data-usage settings; **Tor** simplified (auto-detection removed, "Use Tor" migrates to generic Proxy Settings, **Tor VPN** recommended); the **panic** feature stays; **app hiding simplified to only the icon and name** so users understand the disguise's limits (F-Droid still appears in Apps settings and is detectable in forensic inspection); the **app-wipe** feature (e.g. via the Ripple panic trigger) has **not returned** (specialized maintenance, small user base — users relying on it may postpone updating); **FPE is not supported by 2.0** which focuses on Android's **session installer** for background updates without it; OSes integrating F-Droid (CalyxOS, emteriaOS, iodéOS, Lineage-for-microG, ShiftOS) use additional repos. Under the hood: Kotlin + **Jetpack Compose**, closer to Material Design, **lowering the contributor barrier** and building a foundation for the next decade; support for **Android 6 was dropped** (a needed fix landed in Android 7) though old F-Droid releases still work on old Android. Funding: Torsten Grote's work via **NLnet/Mobifree**; **OTF UX & Discovery Lab** + **Ura Design** for user research/design; OTF FOSS Sustainability Fund, NGI, Mobifree, Calyx Institute; **OTF Security Lab + Convocation** independent security review. **Nearby** (serverless device-to-device app sharing) is being rebuilt on improved connection methods, not ready yet. Takeaways: (1) the install-experience gain comes from **antitrust/DMA pressure, not goodwill** — without regulation third-party stores stay second-class on Android; (2) Kotlin+Compose is a **strategic bet on lowering maintenance cost** for the next decade (cost: dropping Android 6, but old releases still work); (3) the privacy-feature trade-offs expose the **low-base/high-cost dilemma** of open-source projects, handled with honest boundary-setting and a downgrade path; (4) the backdrop is Google tightening sideloading vs the DMA forcing openness — F-Droid 2.0 lands in that window.
  - Key topics: F-Droid, Android, open-source app store, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material Design, DMA, Digital Markets Act, sideloading, privacy, app hiding, panic feature, Tor VPN, FPE, session installer, Nearby, CalyxOS, LineageOS, NLnet, Mobifree, Open Technology Fund
- [当软件订阅变成公共政策：一座城市的 70 万美元软件账单](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-24_software-subscriptions-public-policy/): Translation+analysis of O'Reilly Radar (Steve Hayes, 2026-09-24). A conversation with **Dan Gookin** — author of 1991's *DOS For Dummies* (the book that launched the *For Dummies* series; 180+ tech books, 12M+ copies) and now mayor of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho — becomes a bigger question: what happens when the software you *rent* becomes infrastructure you can't leave? Gookin: "Our software subscription just for our city, our size, is **$700,000 a year and growing**." His recurring example is the city's finance software — once *owned*, now leased and cloud-based — prompting: **"So we don't even own our own data?"** His worry isn't literal legal ownership but *practical control*: if the vendor is hacked or the city switches, can it get all its data back — "a binary dump" or the actual data? Gookin floats hiring a couple of contract programmers to rebuild in-house ("then we own it again"); Hayes is unconvinced: two programmers can't reproduce a mature municipal finance system, endpoint protection, records management and public-safety apps (let alone compliance and vendor support); AI-accelerated development adds liability/security risk a government likely won't accept in the name of ownership; in-house software creates its own long-term bills (maintenance, patching, staff/framework turnover); and an app you write can be **every bit as hard to escape as one you buy**. Conversely, replacing a "good enough" system with a packaged one that fits most-but-not-all of your needs can cost more than keeping the old one — build-versus-buy exists for good reasons. Still, the question stands: **at what point does the cost of renting capability justify rebuilding some of your own, and which capabilities should an organization insist on controlling even if renting is cheaper?** There's no universal answer, including "the vendor handles it." Hayes explicitly isn't arguing against the cloud — cloud/SaaS solve real problems (shifting maintenance to specialists; giving a 58,000-person city capabilities it could never economically build or maintain). The real question isn't cloud-vs-on-prem or proprietary-vs-open-source but whether you accept **dependency you've consciously chosen vs dependency you've acquired by default**; an org may rationally rent a critical service indefinitely — but it should know where the data lives, how it comes back, what switching would require, and which internal skills have atrophied. Takeaways: (1) at the individual level a subscription is a bill, but for governments/large orgs it's a **sovereignty / public-asset-control** question (public records' accessibility, portability and auditability bear on accountability); (2) the sharpest line is chosen-vs-default dependency, which escapes the cloud/local and open/proprietary binaries — the four questions are essentially an **exit plan** checklist; (3) it de-hypes "just build it yourself" and respects build-vs-buy — autonomy isn't free and isn't automatic, and owning your own code can be paid for in maintenance debt and harder-to-replace lock-in; (4) it rhymes with the broader rise of SaaS data-ownership/exit strategy, contractual data-portability clauses, "you own the code, you own the data" government advocacy, and AI-era context-data portability fights.
  - Key topics: software subscription, SaaS, public policy, vendor lock-in, data portability, exit plan, build vs buy, cloud, open source, government procurement, public records, dependency, O'Reilly Radar, Dan Gookin, Coeur d'Alene
- [C++ 内存排查四件套：ASan / Valgrind / gdb / memleak 架构师级攻略](https://freelamp.com/leisurelinux/articles/0055.html) — 发布于 未知：内存问题只有两种：一种把你炸得粉碎，一种让你慢慢失血。前者好治，后者才是真正的工程难题。——从架构师视角看C++内存排查
- [瀑布模型的荒诞起源：软件工程史上最大的误会](https://freelamp.com/leisurelinux/articles/0131.html) — 发布于 2026-06-21 15:41：一个从未被作者本人主张过的方法论，怎么就成了整个行业的"圣经"？━━━━━━━━━######缘起：1970年的一篇论文
- [别再瞎布 485 线了！从原理到施工，一篇真正讲明白的 485 总线干货](https://freelamp.com/leisurelinux/articles/0424.html) — 发布于 未知

- [长鑫（CXMT）要在北京做 3D NAND：DRAM 一哥，开始踩 YMTC 的 NAND 地盘](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-18_cxmt-3d-nand-rd-beijing/): Translation+analysis of Tom's Hardware / Reuters reports (2026-09-18) that China's top memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) intends to build a 3D NAND R&D production line at its second manufacturing facility near Beijing, leaning on a local Beijing research institute whose remit includes NAND development. The line is R&D + pilot (not a commercial mass-production fab), with start timing and whether pilot work graduates to volume manufacturing still undecided — distinct from the separate Beijing DRAM fab expansion discussed in August. Context: a global memory shortage (AI-server demand) expected to keep supply tight through at least 2027. Domestically CXMT leads DRAM while YMTC anchors NAND; a CXMT NAND push would overlap the two "dual stars" of Chinese memory and add a domestic contender alongside Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron.
  - Key topics: CXMT, ChangXin, 3D NAND, YMTC, Yangtze Memory, SSD, DRAM, semiconductor, domestic memory, Beijing fab, memory shortage
- [Git 2.56 发布，3.0 要把 SHA-256 设为默认：reftable、强制 Rust 与大小写 ID 清除](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-18_git-256-and-30/): Translation+analysis of LWN's report (Jonathan Corbet, 2026-09-18) on Git 2.56 (RC, ~700 non-merge commits, ships late September: new `git history drop <commit>` that replays later commits but still refuses merge-containing histories, `git status` suggesting `git pull`, `git refs` create/delete/update/rename, `git branch --delete-merged`, `git add --resolved` that stages only conflict-resolved paths and aborts on leftover conflict markers, config-lock retry; routine fixes/refactors) and the likely Git 3.0 breaking changes. 3.0 candidates: SHA-256 becomes the default hash (replacing SHA-1; non-experimental since 2.42/2023; GitLab since 2024, Forgejo yes, GitHub the last forge gap but a SHA-256 repo was demoed at git-merge), reftable becomes the default ref storage (replacing `.git/refs` files, solves Android's 800k-ref inefficiency, libgit2 gained reftable support and defaulted SHA-256 in August), object IDs accept only lowercase (kills `f00f00` vs `F00F00` ambiguity bugs/vulns), and Rust becomes a hard build requirement from 3.0 (no-Rust-toolchain platforms can't upgrade; the Rust-free 2.99.x line gets long-term maintenance). Takeaways: the 3.0 breaking set is a single theme — paying down backward-compat debt (security, scale, maintainability, ambiguity removal); the SHA-256 default's real break point is forges not Git, eased by forward opt-in + full support for old SHA-1/reftable-less repos; forced Rust's blast radius is overstated and the 2.99.x line buys time; and the user-visible 2.56 wins are small commands (`history drop`, `add --resolved`, `branch --delete-merged`), with `history drop` still blocked by merges showing how many real histories carry merges.
  - Key topics: Git, version control, 2.56, 3.0, SHA-256, SHA-1, reftable, Rust, breaking changes, object ID case, LWN, Junio Hamano, brian m. carlson
- [CPO 的下一站，可能是一块玻璃：共封装光学走向「玻璃集成平台」](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-21_cpo-glass-integration-platform/): Translation+analysis of SemiWiki's piece (Moh Kolb, 2026-09-21) on co-packaged optics (CPO). CPO is framed as a proximity problem — move the optical engine next to the switch ASIC/XPU to shorten the electrical path, cut SerDes power, raise bandwidth density — but proximity doesn't eliminate the physical bottleneck, it just changes its coordinates in the system. Core thesis: packaging is no longer just supporting the system, it is defining what system can be built, and the substrate under CPO becomes strategic. Glass as an integration platform: good dimensional stability, low-loss high-frequency electrical routing, smooth surface for fine RDL, engineerable CTE, and much larger integration dimensions than wafer-constrained silicon interposers; because optics is geometrically sensitive, dimensional stability becomes an architectural capability. Further: future glass substrates could participate in both electrical and optical integration (TGV vertical vias + on-substrate optics) becoming an integration plane. The critical gate is TGV (through-glass via) manufacturing — via geometry, glass damage, metallization, copper fill, adhesion, residual stress, cracking, long-term reliability; glass is NOT a thermal material (thermal path must be deliberately engineered); and ecosystem (materials, equipment, TGV, fine RDL, KGD strategy, inspection, multi-source supply) matters more than the first demo. Pairs with the CXMT 3D NAND and Huawei 122TB SSD (board-level packaging) stories as the same "packaging breaks process limits / substrate inversion" narrative — advanced packaging is moving from sidekick to architecture definer.
  - Key topics: semiconductor, advanced packaging, CPO, co-packaged optics, glass substrate, TGV, heterogeneous integration, reftable-like ref storage, EIC/PIC, AI package, SemiWiki

- [Oracle 新一轮裁员：6 点清晨邮件、28 亿美元重组，以及 13% 的年度失血](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-14_oracle-layoffs-2-8b-restructuring/): Translation+analysis of TechTimes UK (2026-09-14). Oracle began a new layoff round sending termination emails at 6 a.m. Monday; FY2026 workforce fell ~21,000 (13%) to ~141,000 before this round. Restructuring plan cost raised by $700M to ~$2.8B (severance, contract termination, other costs). Reddit accounts describe a coordinated timeline: federated logins disabled 4 a.m. ET, Slack cut 5–5:30 a.m., emails at 6 a.m. sharp. Email text quoted ("today is your last working day"). Oracle has not said whether AI is absorbing eliminated roles and made no public comment on the round. Business Standard names Oracle/Amazon/Dell/Uber/PayPal as drivers of 2026 global layoffs.
  - Key topics: Oracle, layoffs, restructuring, $2.8B, workforce reduction, AI investment, TechTimes UK

## Quick Reference

### Linux TLS/PKI Commands
```bash
# Import private CA to system trust store (Debian/Ubuntu)
cp internal_ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/
update-ca-certificates

# Verify certificate hash index
openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -hash

# Check Java trust store
keytool -list -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts

# Test TLS with custom CA bundle
curl --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt https://internal.service.local
```

Without an FCC Conditional Approval, vendors are effectively barred from selling new wireless hardware in the US, so previously certified Wi-Fi 7 gear can still be sold while any new Wi-Fi 7 or Wi-Fi 8 product is locked out; TP-Link's move to incorporate TP-Link Systems in California is being challenged in legal filings. Specs: Broadcom Wi-Fi 8 chipset, up to 33 percent more real-world throughput than TP-Link's own Wi-Fi 7 hardware and 24 percent more consistent throughput under high interference, two auto-sensing 10 Gbps WAN/LAN ports, four 2.5 Gbps LAN ports, 3,600 sq ft coverage, 200 devices. Also covers the caveats that Wi-Fi 8 (802.11bn) is not yet ratified and this ships against a draft, so the upgrade only pays off once endpoints catch up.

### 机器凭据轮换只是买时间：ZSP 的关键不在「换密码」，在「有没有人负责关掉它」
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_zero-standing-privilege-machine-identities/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: 安全/运维
Source: CSO Online（Ashish Mishra，Opinion）+ Google Threat Intelligence Group / Palo Alto Networks / Entro Labs 一手数据
Summary: 解读 CSO Online 评论文章关于「零常驻特权」（ZSP）的论证，并逐条回溯它引用的三组调研数据。核心判断：轮换（rotation）改的是凭据的值，撤销（revocation）改的是凭据的有效性，而这两件事在机器凭据场景里可以完全脱钩，因为没有人会「重新登录」。文章追溯 2025 年 8 月 Salesloft Drift 事件（UNC6395 用被窃 OAuth 令牌从 700+ 家组织的 Salesforce 实例导出数据，目的是搜寻 AWS AKIA 密钥、密码和 Snowflake 令牌），并补上原文未展开的对照组：Okta 靠入站 IP 限制和 DPoP 挡住了同一次攻击，说明「令牌约束」比「令牌轮换」更接近答案。另指出原文最锋利的一句是「一个没有归属人的账号，往往能熬过每一次清理行动，因为没有人有权力批准关掉它」，以及 Entro Labs 那组对照数据（机器凭据 7.5% 寿命 5-10 年 vs 人类员工任职期中位数 3.9 年）。
Key topics: 零常驻特权, ZSP, zero standing privilege, 机器身份, NHI, 非人类身份, 服务账号, OAuth, refresh token, 令牌重放, bearer token, 令牌约束, DPoP, mTLS, IP 白名单, Salesloft Drift, UNC6395, Salesforce 数据窃取, AWS AKIA, Snowflake 令牌, PAM, 工作负载身份联合, OIDC, GitHub Actions, 动态机密, 凭据轮换, 凭据撤销, 109:1, 144:1, Entro Labs, Palo Alto Networks 2026 Identity Security Landscape, Okta

### PwnEscape：一个 17 年的内核 bug，AI 用 3 天找到，而修复只堵了 5 个消费点
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_pwnescape-cve-2026-99999-linux-networking-vm-escape/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: 安全/运维
Source: pwn.ai 原始技术报告 + Linux 内核 commit 6785011f8b16 原始补丁 + CSO Online 报道 + NVD
Summary: CVE-2026-99999（PwnEscape，CVSS 9.3）是一个 guest-to-host 逃逸漏洞，但根因不在 hypervisor，而在 Linux 网络栈：guest 控制的校验和元数据（csum_start + csum_offset）可以授权一次对包内存的延迟写入，而这次写入正好落在 IPv4 头部的 IHL 字段上，把头部长度从 20 字节改成 60 字节。文章拆解了那个「32 字节」的算术（逻辑线性头 28 字节 = 20 字节头 + 8 字节载荷，声称 60 字节 → 60-28=32 字节被当成 IPv4 选项发出），并引用报告的克制表述：「这里的越界指的是 sk_buff 的合法逻辑线性包数据，而不一定是对整个分配器对象的访问越界」。修复 commit 6785011f8b16（Michael S. Tsirkin）是一个 44 行补丁，加 7 行 ip_check_csum_start() 助手并在 5 个消费点调用，commit message 自述「作为一层纵深防御措施……更完整的输入侧校验即将到来，但需要更多工作」。另分析 AI 在研究中的角色：Omega-Pwn + GPT-5.6 Sol，3 天找到原语、API 成本低于 700 美元，但报告明确声明「我们用这个循环去搜索一个更大的空间，而不降低证明的标准」，并用五级证据阶梯区分「源码假设/受控变异/主机内存泄露/选择性内核写入/自有机器上的受限执行」。
Key topics: PwnEscape, CVE-2026-99999, Linux 内核漏洞, 虚拟机逃逸, guest-to-host escape, KVM escape, Firecracker, Vercel Sandbox, 校验和卸载, checksum offload, CHECKSUM_PARTIAL, sk_buff, csum_start, csum_offset, skb_checksum_help, IPv4 IHL, ip_do_fragment, TOCTOU, 延迟元数据信任反转, deferred-metadata trust inversion, Michael S. Tsirkin, Willem de Bruijn, AI 辅助漏洞研究, Omega-Pwn, OmegaClaw, GPT-5.6 Sol, 证据阶梯

### 「Flatpak 是一团安全噩梦」：原文写于 2023 年，而 2026 年的两个证据它都没等到
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_flatpak-sandbox-security-debate-flatkill-rebuttal/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: Linux/运维
Source: oro.gay 博客（Yves Auxier，2023-06-15）+ flatkill.org 原始批评 + CVE-2026-34078 GitHub 安全公告 + Flatpak/Flathub 官方文档 + ArchWiki
Summary: 解读一篇 2023 年反驳 flatkill.org 的文章，其核心论证是「Flatpak 是沙箱。而 Flatpak 是安全的。应用不是。」文章指出这场打了八年的争论没有结论，是因为双方在回答两个不同的问题（「我这个 app 实际能干什么」vs「沙箱机制是否成立」），而原文自己给出了双方唯一能达成一致的事实陈述：「当前的 API 还不够完善」。文章补上原文没等到的两个 2026 年证据：① CVE-2026-34078（CVSS 9.3，2026-04，修复于 1.16.4）是一个「完整的沙箱逃逸，导致主机文件访问和主机上下文中的代码执行」，根因是门户对 sandbox-expose 路径的符号链接处理，后果与授予应用的权限无关，恰好落在原文框架之外；② ArchWiki 至今在 Flatpak 条目警告「Flathub 上很多 Flatpak 应用默认并没有被有效地沙箱化」，并给出最终答案：「运行不受信任的代码永远是不安全的；沙箱化不能改变这一点。」另指出原文用「无关紧要」跳过了 flatkill 关于应用捆绑库滞后的具体指控（VSCode/Android Studio/Sublime Text 里的 git 2.9.3），也几乎没碰「沙箱图标误导用户」这一条，而三年后恰恰是那条最经得起检验。
Key topics: Flatpak, 沙箱安全, flatkill.org, Flathub, Portals, 静态权限, filesystem=host, filesystem=home, device=all, Flatseal, CVE-2026-34078, CVE-2026-34079, 符号链接逃逸, TheEvilSkeleton, fractureiser, PrismLauncher, 桌面 Linux, 应用分发, 打包格式, ArchWiki, 运行时, freedesktop SDK, 最小权限

### TEE 的漏洞清单已经长得能写进一篇博客：而作者最狠的一句是「打断一台等于打断全部」
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_tee-attestation-forgery-threat-model/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: 安全/运维
Source: Alin Tomescu 博客（2026-10-11）+ TEE.fail / WireTap / BadRAM 原始论文 + Intel 官方公告 2025-10-28-001 + Intel PCK 规范
Summary: 解读 Alin Tomescu 的 763 词 TEE 攻击清单，核心论证是「你的远程证明验签器接受任何一台处于良好状态的 Intel CPU 的 quote，而攻击者的 CPU 就是其中一台。打断一台就是打断全部」。文章拆解了这个论证的机制（每个 CPU 封装有唯一 PCK，但所有 PCK 证书都由 Intel 签发并公开可取，所以验签通过意味着「Intel 真的为一个攻击者控制的密钥签过证书」），并补上原文没写的三个事实：① 这类内存总线插入攻击成本低于 1000 美元、用二手设备即可（BadRAM 重编程 DIMM 约 10 美元）；② Intel 的官方公告明确表示 TEE.fail「并没有改变 Intel 之前对这类物理攻击的『不在范围内』声明」；③ 真正的架构变化不是新攻击，而是 TEE 从 enclave 转向机密虚拟机时「移除了完整性保证和对重放攻击的保护」，而「大多数 TEE 部署似乎没有意识到安全保证上的差别」。另指出 TEE.fail 证明密钥还能攻破 Nvidia GPU 机密计算，且「TDX 的安全性实际上依赖 SGX 来提供证明」。结论给出可操作分工：TEE 只做纵深防御，隐私给 TEE、完整性给 ZKP。
Key topics: TEE, 可信执行环境, SGX, TDX, SEV-SNP, Nitro Enclaves, 远程证明, remote attestation, PCK, Provisioning Certification Key, PCK 固定, 证明伪造, 侧信道, 物理攻击, 内存总线插入, WireTap, TEE.fail, BadRAM, DDRop, Battering RAM, Foreshadow, SGAxe, ÆPIC Leak, Signal 通讯录 enclave, 机密计算, 机密虚拟机, CVM, 确定性加密, Nvidia GPU 机密计算, Alin Tomescu, Sanctum, ZKP, MPC, 威胁模型, footgun

### 二十五年的「NSA 后门」疑云解开了：而答案是一个 Unix 时间戳加上一个 1990 年代的随机数生成器
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_nist-ecdsa-curve-seeds-lrand48-timestamp/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: 安全/运维
Source: Anthropic 官方研究文章（2026-10-16）+ 可运行复现代码
Summary: NIST 椭圆曲线的「种子」自 2000 年 FIPS 186-2 起就来源不明，由 NSA 提供且无任何解释，是密码学界悬了二十五年的公开疑问。2026 年 10 月，一位 Anthropic 员工在未告知「幽默短语哈希」这条线索的情况下询问内部研究模型，Claude 在半小时内解出答案：这些种子不是任何哈希的输出，而是 1990 年代 C 库随机数生成器 lrand48 的输出，用 Unix 时间戳做种子。关键证据是十个种子里有四个的所有 20 个字的高位都是 0（巧合概率 1/5,810），这是 lrand48 只返回 48 位状态高 31 位的签名；素数域曲线用 LLL 格约简从被截断的 LCG 恢复状态，倒推 `srand48` 形式（低 16 位 = 0x330E）后解出十个时间戳全部落在 1997 年 5 月到 1998 年 4 月之间。文章还顺手解开第二个谜：1997 年 5 月生成的那六条曲线的基准点来自 FreeLIP 的随机数生成器（种子 20000、20420 等，丢弃七个输出），这是首次有任何 NIST 基准点被解释。Anthropic 明确声明这不是破解或弱点，反而降低了「被人为挑选」的可能性；另有三个未解缺口（B-163 种子、四个大素数域曲线的基准点、二元域曲线的基准点）和一处需谨慎的发现（有潜在可行候选被跳过）。悬赏 36,864 美元捐给 Internet Security Research Group（Let's Encrypt 背后组织）。
Key topics: ECDSA, 椭圆曲线, NIST, FIPS 186-2, lrand48, srand48, 0x330E, 种子, seed, P-192, P-224, P-256, P-384, P-521, ANSI X9.62, 素数域, 二元域, LLL, 格约简, 线性同余生成器, LCG, 截断LCG, FreeLIP, NTL, Arjen Lenstra, Jerry Solinas, Bob Reiter, Koblitz, Menezes, A Riddle Wrapped in an Enigma, Dual_EC_DRBG, 后门疑云, 可验证随机性, Claude, Anthropic, Internet Security Research Group

### Gentoo 给 Chromium 做了「临终祷告」：而杀死这个打包的是一句「这太荒唐了」
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_gentoo-chromium-last-rites-maintainer-burnout/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: Linux/运维
Source: LWN.net（Joe Brockmeier，2026-10-06）+ Gentoo Bugzilla 原始对话
Summary: Gentoo 于 2026-09-24 为 www-client/chromium 宣布「临终祷告」（last rites），即放弃维护并从仓库屏蔽该包（用户升级会被警告挡住，临终祷告期到 10-24）。表面导火索是稳定版 151.0.7922.169 落后且「包含 602 个已知漏洞」，而 LWN 还原的完整对话显示真正触发点是报障者 Roman Žilka 说「这太荒唐了」，维护者 Sam James 回「那就这样吧」。文章梳理双方立场与那组关键数字：维护者称 Chromium「轻松就是 Gentoo 里消耗维护者最多的包」，每周要花六小时以上（只算快机上的编译时间），需要至少三个人（现在只有他从 2023 年起一个人扛），技能要求横跨 C/C++/Go/JavaScript/Rust 加一堆「永远没法在别处用上」的 Google 自有工具；用户实测单次编译 15 到 16 小时，所以无法测所有 USE 标签组合。上游问题是结构性的：加了 Go 依赖、用会在新版本崩溃的实验性 Rust 特性、发布 tarball 的 CI 不可靠且「他们似乎没有注意到或在意」、不用可选功能被禁用来测试构建、官方「如何从源码构建 Linux 版」的文档链接返回 503。文章还记下那句最精辟的判断「复制 ebuild 在它失效之前都工作得很好」，以及对三种挽救方案（降级为尽力而为、用别人 overlay、砍掉 USE 灵活性）的逐个拒绝理由。
Key topics: Gentoo, Chromium, 打包, ebuild, Portage, USE标签, last rites, 临终祷告, orphan, 维护者倦怠, Sam James, Matt Jolly, Roman Žilka, www-client/chromium, 602个CVE, -bundled-toolchain, overlay, Bentoo, Freeburn, Binhost, Flatpak, Fedora, Debian, 发布节奏, CI不可靠, 开源治理, 志愿者

### 同一个活，两种引擎：一个 100GB 的教训，把 OLTP 换成 lakehouse 到底换掉了什么
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_innodb-vs-iceberg-olap-migration-internals/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: 数据/运维
Source: marcpau.io 技术复盘（Marc Paul，2026-09-14），含作者自建系统的完整 DDL/MERGE/存储过程
Summary: 作者把自己的股票分析系统从 MySQL/InnoDB 迁到 Iceberg + Spark + Polaris + MinIO，并逐项对照两个引擎的内部机制。迁移动机只有一个优化：指标表有 36 列，而分析通常只需 2 到 3 列，他付出了「大约 8,000 字和 9 个月」的代价换到列裁剪。文章拆解 InnoDB 的三个保证（行存所有列、索引加快读减慢写、undo log 实现 MVCC）如何各自在分析场景变成负担，以及 Iceberg 的「俄罗斯套娃」三层剪枝（Parquet 行组统计 → Manifest 含分区值 → Manifest List 含分区版本，支撑 split planning）。两种原子提交恰好相反：v1 用咨询锁让第二个写入者排队，v2 用乐观指针交换让失败者重做。MVCC 的对照最干净：「InnoDB 保存旧的行的版本……而 Iceberg 跳过了保存，因为旧版本就是旧文件。」还保留了他承认的最糟设计：日期只放在主表里导致所有指标表要 join 回主表，直到数据库超过 100GB 才发现，而根源是他「当时甚至不知道最重要的价格是收盘价」。两处未修的债：44 个退役的 metadata.json（忘了配过期策略）和还没加 WRITE ORDERED BY。
Key topics: InnoDB, Iceberg, OLTP, OLAP, lakehouse, MySQL, Spark, Polaris, MinIO, Parquet, Avro, manifest, manifest list, metadata.json, 三层剪枝, split planning, 行组, MVCC, undo log, history list, copy-on-write, merge-on-read, delete file, 快照, 乐观并发, 咨询锁, 列式存储, 分区, bucket, compaction, snapshot expiration, 数据建模, 量化分析, WRITE ORDERED BY

### 想下载一个 ISO，最后写了个内核漏洞利用程序：而他只需要往两个 sysfs 文件里写两个零
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_tplink-eap770-dma-cache-bug-kernel-exploit/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: 安全/运维
Source: deafbeef 博客技术复盘（2026-10-10），含高通驱动源码具体行号与完整利用链
Summary: 作者的 TP-Link EAP770 v1（高通 IPQ9574，Linux 5.4.164）在 Wi-Fi 下载时损坏数据，两年里他依次排除了 rsync/SSH（Wireshark 显示零错误校验和零重传）、笔记本网卡（换卡仍复现）、线缆（有线客户端干净）、空口（坏帧的 CCMP MIC 完整）。转折点是抓到「1440 字节段里有连续 64 个字节错误而 TCP 校验和有效」，由此推出「有东西在损坏之后重算了校验和」，而 64 字节正好是缓存行，最后锁定唯一「既加速桥接又重算校验和」的东西：高通 SFE/PPE 卸载。根因在 qca-nss-dp：快速发送路径只 clean skb_headlen(skb) 字节就设 fast_recycled=1 把缓冲区放回回收链表，接收侧看到该标志就跳过 dmac_inv_range_no_dsb，而接收区是 1856 字节（29 个缓存行）从 head+192 开始，发送侧只清理了另一偏移的 2 到 3 行，脏行回写覆盖 64 字节包内容；arm64 的 __dma_inv_area 对边缘行用 dc civac（clean and invalidate）更让「invalidate」这个直觉失效。修复只需 echo 0 到两个 sysfs 文件，但 TP-Link 的 SSH 是 uid 1 无 capabilities，于是他写了 CVE-2022-0185 + 管道缓冲区伪造的利用链拿 root，约 17 小时、每次启动只有一次机会、kallsyms 被清零、各段偏移不一致。代价是 8% 下载速度。文章还记下 Opus 5.5 的护栏每两条消息切断一次会话、Cyber Verification Program 无效，以及他在其他驱动里发现同类 DMA 缓存维护问题（x86 上因硬件一致性而不复现，OpenWrt 无此 bug）。
Key topics: TP-Link, EAP770, Qualcomm, IPQ9574, DMA, 缓存一致性, cache coherency, SFE, PPE, qca-nss-dp, edma_tx.c, edma_rx.c, skb_recycler, fast_recycled, dmac_clean_range, dmac_inv_range, dc civac, CHECKSUM_UNNECESSARY, TcpInCsumErrors, CVE-2022-0185, legacy_parse_param, modprobe_path, request_module, pipe buffer, anon_pipe_buf_ops, generic_pipe_buf_confirm, KASLR, kallsyms, arm64, x86 DMA 一致性, Wi-Fi 7, 闭源固件, amss.bin, ath12k, 设备EOL, OpenWrt

### 为了让这台 128GB 的 RTX Spark 笔记本跑 Linux，她自己写了 ACPI 覆盖和触控板补丁
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_rtx-spark-laptop-arch-linux-arm-nvidia/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: Linux/运维
Source: josie.lol 实测（作者为 Arch Linux 官方打包者）+ NVIDIA 官方规格页与驱动 README + Arch Linux ARM 包索引
Summary: ASUS ProArt P16（RTX Spark N1X，6,144 CUDA 核心 + 20 核 Grace CPU + 128GB 统一内存，NVIDIA 官方只标 Windows 11）被作者跑上 Arch Linux ARM，代价是自己补四层东西：修 ACPI override 分配与 framebuffer 映射拿到控制台、从笔记本自己的表推导 ACPI 覆盖、打补丁的 hid-asus 支持键盘、写音频 machine driver，固件从 ASUS 驱动包本地提取。三组实测数据：① 7-Zip 单线程与 Windows HP OmniBook 基本平手（压缩 −1.2%、解压 −0.8%），20 线程快 5.0% 和 2.7%，并用 ComputerBase 的独立测试交叉验证落在 155.759 到 157.193 GIPS 区间内；② 内存是 116.0 GiB 同时报告为系统 RAM 和 CUDA 总量（Windows 分三个互不相通区域，91 GiB 预留时 CUDA 总量 109.7 GiB），作者最在意的不是多 6.3 GiB 而是「不用在工作负载之间移动预留滑块并重启」；③ vLLM 跑 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4 加载 68.2 GiB 模型 + 21.1 GiB KV cache，生成约 30.9 tokens/s 与 Windows 的 llama.cpp 相当，十分钟 150 个请求延迟增长不到 1.6%。本文补上一个作者没明说的关键前提：NVIDIA README 明确「Blackwell 及之后的架构只被开源内核模块支持」，所以这次移植成功有一半要归功于 NVIDIA 2022 年的转向，而那转向的动因是技术性的（HMM、DMABUF、confidential computing 需要与内核深度集成），不是道德性的。

### ACPI 覆盖到底怎么做：从作者的仓库里拆出完整流程，以及哪些部分能迁移到你自己的笔记本
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-19_acpi-table-override-guide-initrd-cpio/
Date: 2026-10-19
Category: Linux/运维
Source: pfeifferj/archlinuxarm-proart-p16 仓库源码逐文件阅读（MIT，386 文件）+ ACPI 规范与内核表覆盖机制
Summary: 一份可操作的 ACPI 表覆盖指南，全部流程来自 RTX Spark 移植项目仓库的实际代码。核心机制：ACPI 覆盖不是改固件，而是让内核在早期启动时用 initrd 里 /kernel/firmware/acpi/ 下的 DSDT.aml、SSDT.aml 替换固件表（开关 CONFIG_ACPI_TABLE_UPGRADE），即「在 RAM 中应用，不要刷固件」。dump 给了两条路线：UEFI Shell 下 acpiview -s DSDT -d（适用于 Linux 起不来），或从 /sys/firmware/acpi/tables 直接 cat（前提是本次启动未加载覆盖，否则 dump 到的是覆盖表而非固件原表）。改动阶段是全部难度所在，作者的两个关键决定是：① 只改 6 个方法的缓冲区生命周期（把局部变量 Local0/Local5 换成命名对象 RSPB），因为「编译整张表会重写无关的 AML」，所以做法是只把编译后的方法字节拼接回原始 SSDT；② 精确打掉一处 _OSI("Windows 2022") 谓词（替换为 Noop 0xa3）而不是用全局 acpi_osi=，因为后者会让所有依赖 _OSI 的地方都走 Windows 分支。拼接代码的严谨性值得学：每段替换校验哈希、外层 Scope/Device 的 package length 同步改、变长编码宽度变化会被拒绝、从后往前替换防偏移失效、最后重算校验和并自检。另记录一个少人知道的陷阱：替换 DSDT 跨过 EFI 描述符边界时，内核早期映射接受但后期 acpi_os_ioremap() 拒绝，报 AE_NO_ACPI_TABLES 导致 USB/NVMe/GPU 全部无法枚举；作者的内核补丁增加 arch_alloc_acpi_tables() 钩子，只在单个 conventional+WB+非runtime 的 EFI 描述符内分配，无跨描述符回退。文章最后区分了可迁移（dump 方法、路径约定、只改方法不重编译、精确 _OSI、版本哈希绑定）与不可迁移（具体的 ASUS EC 方法名、字节偏移、ARM64 allocator 补丁），并给出最小可行路径：争取做成「等长替换」以避免处理 package length 的变长编码。
Key topics: ACPI, DSDT, SSDT, ACPI 表覆盖, CONFIG_ACPI_TABLE_UPGRADE, initrd, initramfs, cpio, 070701, TRAILER, kernel/firmware/acpi, acpiview, acpidump, UEFI Shell, EDK2, iasl, ACPICA, AML, MethodOp, package length, 变长编码, Scope, Device, _OSI, acpi_osi, Noop 0xa3, SSPM, NVDA8400, EC 嵌入式控制器, Local0, Local5, 命名对象, 缓冲区生命周期, EFI 内存描述符, EFI_CONVENTIONAL_MEMORY, EFI_MEMORY_WB, memblock, acpi_os_ioremap, AE_NO_ACPI_TABLES, arch_alloc_acpi_tables, ACPI_TABLE_UPGRADE_MAX_PHYS, MEMBLOCK_ALLOC_ACCESSIBLE, ARM64, 笔记本, 固件版本绑定

### Secure Boot 证书到期：真正的问题不是「证书过期」，而是「更新信任的钥匙，锁在被更新的那把锁里」
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-20_secure-boot-certificate-expiration-2026-kek-gating/
Date: 2026-10-20
Category: 系统/硬件
Source: 微软 KB 5062710 / KB 5079373 官方原文 + Red Hat / AlmaLinux / Rocky Linux 官方说明 + Microsoft Linux 博客 + CERT VU#616257 + 本机 efivars 实测
Summary: 微软三张 2011 年 Secure Boot 证书在 2026 年陆续到期（KEK CA 2011 = 6月24日，Microsoft UEFI CA 2011 = 6月27日，Windows Production PCA 2011 = 10月19日），而媒体几乎只报了最后一个日期。本文指出真正的架构问题是 KEK 门控：KEK 的职责是授权对 db 和 dbx 的变更，而 KEK 自己也在过期清单里，所以「没拿到 2023 KEK 的设备没有权限接收携带 2023 证书的那个 db 更新」，形成递归依赖，只能靠固件更新或已签好的更新包绕开。文章梳理三张证书的分工（含 Microsoft UEFI CA 2011 被拆成 bootloader 与 Option ROM 两个新证书）、澄清「到期 ≠ 吊销」（Secure Boot 验证签名看信任库与吊销状态，不看有效期，所以反直觉地不应该删掉 2011 CA），并给出三种而非两种实际状态：① 已有 2023；② 有 2011 在等更新；③ 固件里连生效的信任库都没配、默认库仍是 2011 版。第三种状态由作者在 H3CBook Ultra 14T 物理机上实测得出：efivars 只有 5 个变量且全是 *Default（属性 0x06），dbDefault 里只有 2011 证书、无任何 2023。Linux 侧给出不同的处境：到期不影响已签发 shim 启动，真正的风险是发行版发布「只由 2023 签署」的 shim 时旧固件会启动失败，因此现在全在发双签名 shim；同时 dbx 确实被追溯性地加入了 11 个有漏洞的 shim（CVE-2026-8863，shim 0.9 及更早，类似 BYOVD 绕过 Secure Boot）。另指出一个几乎没人提的副作用：改 db 会改变 PCR7，从而导致 BitLocker 或 TPM-LUKS 进恢复模式，Red Hat 的建议是先用不变的 PCR 重新封装再对新 PCR7 封装。
Key topics: Secure Boot, UEFI, 证书到期, KEK, Key Exchange Key, KEK CA 2011, KEK 2K CA 2023, db, dbx, PK, PKDefault, dbDefault, Setup Mode, User Mode, Windows Production PCA 2011, Windows UEFI CA 2023, Microsoft UEFI CA 2011, Microsoft Option ROM UEFI CA 2023, 到期 vs 吊销, CVE-2026-8863, shim, 双签名, shim 0.9, BYOVD, SBAT, AlmaLinux, RHEL, Rocky Linux, mokutil, fwupd, efivars, PCR7, BitLocker 恢复密钥, TPM, Windows 事件 ID 1801, 1808, TPM-WMI, older boot trust configuration

### Magento 六周内第二个满分漏洞：而真正的分水岭不在 CVSS 10.0，在「Adobe 的 priority 1 只留给正在被打的洞」
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-20_magento-blockstrap-cve-2026-103849-priority-2/
Date: 2026-10-20
Category: 安全/运维
Source: Sansec 原始研究（BlockStrap + StyleSmuggler）+ Adobe APSB26-153/APSB26-146 + NVD CVE 记录
Summary: Magento 与 Adobe Commerce 六周内出现第二个 CVSS 10.0 的未认证 RCE（BlockStrap，CVE-2026-103849，CWE-1336 模板注入），Adobe 给 priority 2、30 天窗口，引发争议。本文指出争议问错了方向：Adobe 在社区 Slack 说明 priority 1 只保留给「已知正在被利用」的漏洞，而 priority 衡量紧迫性、CVSS 衡量严重性，两个维度在「未认证 RCE 但还没人打」这个组合下会分歧，所以这个组合在逻辑上不矛盾。真正被 CVSS 数字盖住的是三件事：① 前一个洞 StyleSmuggler（CVE-2026-75650，同样 10.0）从出洞到大规模利用只用 3 天，Sansec 明说 BlockStrap「复杂度相似」，所以「还没被打」是个会快速过期的状态；② Magento Open Source 2.4.6 及更老版本没有公开补丁——Adobe 公开的 10 月补丁只覆盖 2.4.7-p10/2.4.8-p5/2.4.9，2.4.4-p18/2.4.5-p17/2.4.6-p15 的补丁需要 Adobe Commerce 商业许可证；③「普通 composer install 修不了这个洞」，必须装 2026-oct 发行版或隔离补丁。技术机制上，BlockStrap 是「第二遍指令注入」，暴露了 9 月 StyleSmuggler 修复（给受信任指令签名）留下的缺口：子模板里攻击者控制的数据仍可被签名并在根层级重新扫描，夹带的 {{block}} 指令被执行；Adobe 10 月的修法是用注册占位符替换通用重扫描。文章还记录：两个补丁必须都装且 9 月热修要先装（Adobe 的补丁注册表没把它列为前置条件）；验证不能只看构建结果，因为 composer patch 插件可跳过 hunk 而不失败、部署脚本的 `patch || true` 会吞掉失败；StyleSmuggler 的后门是 Rust 程序，C2 伪装成 NTP（48 字节 UDP 到 123 端口，只有前 4 字节真是 NTP）。另指出 AI 辅助逆向如何压缩窗口：改变的不是所需技能，而是时间。
Key topics: Magento, Adobe Commerce, Magento Open Source, BlockStrap, CVE-2026-103849, StyleSmuggler, CVE-2026-75650, CVSS 10.0, 未认证 RCE, 模板注入, SSTI, CWE-1336, second-pass directive injection, 第二遍指令注入, APSB26-153, APSB26-146, VULN-39341, priority 1, priority 2, 补丁窗口, Sansec, vozec, Mage-OS, 3.5.0, 3.6.0, resolveDeferredDirectives, magento-patches, 隔离补丁, composer patch, Adobe Commerce 许可证, 后门, NTP 伪装, MessagePack, 99.84.67.186, 185.157.160.251, ntp.timesync.to, 凭证轮换, 加密密钥轮换, AI辅助逆向

### OpenBSD 8.0 发了：而这次最值得看的不是漏洞修复清单，是内核虚拟地址空间从 4G 跳到 512G
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-20_openbsd-8-0-release-kernel-address-space/
Date: 2026-10-20
Category: Linux/运维
Source: OpenBSD 官方 8.0 发布页（一手，逐项原文摘录）
Summary: OpenBSD 8.0 于 2026-10-20 发布，是第 61 个版本。本文没有逐条罗列，而是挑出三条真正改变系统边界的改动。① amd64 内核虚拟地址空间从 4G 提升到 512G（128 倍），而同页另一条说明它解锁了什么：「amd64 上增加的核虚拟地址空间允许映射超过 4GB 的显存」。这两条是配套的：Arc A 系列显存 6–16GB，在 4G 上限下根本跑不起来，所以「支持 Intel Arc A 系列（DG2/Alchemist）」的前提是地址空间先扩容。而 pmap 直接映射同时被移到随机位置，等于给内核漏洞利用增加难度。② arm64 首次加入休眠支持，而真正的工作量在恢复路径的防御性检查（针对整数溢出校验镜像大小、防止 unhibernate 读取 chunktable 时越界、unhibernate 后清理 framebuffer）——因为 hibernate 镜像是磁盘上保存全部内存内容的文件。③ DRM 更新到 Linux 6.18.53，跟随节奏相当紧。安全侧挑出三条信号最强的：unveil 扩到 man(1)/makewhatis(8)/man.cgi(8)（对公网开放的 CGI 被限制在几个目录，不依赖输入过滤是否完美）；syspatch 加固对抗恶意脚本 + fw_update 检查本地 SHA256.sig 签名 + tar 跳过预期位置之外的文件（防路径穿越，且以 root 运行）；OpenSSH 10.6「把一些关键的公钥解析和验证路径从预认证攻击面中移除」——减少而非加固，是结构性改进。另记一条退役：loongson（早期 MIPS）因 Clang 22 不工作而放弃，而 luna88k 反而有 5 条改进，说明「小众架构」和「被退役的架构」取决于有没有人维护。文末说明用户给的两条链接指向同一页面（t.co 短链的响应体就是跳到 openbsd.org/80.html 的 JS/Meta 跳转）。
Key topics: OpenBSD 8.0, 内核虚拟地址空间, KVA, 4G 到 512G, pmap 直接映射随机化, VRAM 映射, inteldrm, Intel Arc A 系列, DG2, Alchemist, Alder Lake GuC timeout, DRM, Linux 6.18.53, arm64 休眠, hibernate, unhibernate, piglet, framebuffer 残留, Galaxy Book4 Edge, HONOR MagicBook Art 14, ufshci, RISC-V, V 向量扩展, imsic, aplic, Sstc, AT_HWCAP, sparc64 LLVM, loongson 退役, Clang 22, luna88k, pledge, unveil, man.cgi, syspatch, fw_update, SHA256.sig, 路径穿越, OpenSSH 10.6, 预认证攻击面, mldsa44-ed25519, ML-DSA, 后量子, DisableForwarding, PermitTunnel, libsodium, LibreSSL 4.4.0, ML-KEM, ecdh_compute_key, vmm 64 VCPU, x2apic, checksum offload, libexpat 2.8.4, CVE-2026-12087, nsd, LibXfont, sudo 1.9.17p2

Summary: PHP 安全团队于 2026-10-20 发布罕见的提前公告：10 月 21 日 14:00 UTC 将发布两个 CVSS v4.0 9.2 的严重漏洞补丁（外部流传编号 CVE-2026-109618 与 CVE-2026-109619，NVD 写作时暂无记录）。本文指出 LWN 那一段短讯漏掉了两个关键信息：一是「两个」漏洞而非一个，二是官方写明「如果任何一个漏洞的细节被公开，或出现野外利用证据，我们保留提前发布的权利」——这句话说明写公告时就预期细节会泄露，所以这份提前公告本身是应急产物而非流程改进，用户拿到的准备窗口是「一天」而不是「一周」。文章还记下 CVSS 分数偏差（泄露报告里有 10.0，官方口径 9.2），以及真正的难点不在打补丁而在版本可见性：只有 8.2/8.3/8.4/8.5 会被修，8.2 在两个月后 EOL，8.0/8.1 已无补丁，5/6/7 早已 EOL，「补丁发布之后你依然脆弱」；操作系统过保也会导致收不到补丁；而最常见的技术陷阱是 CLI 的 PHP 版本不等于 FPM 池实际加载的版本。最后给出比「立即升级」更具体的准备动作：提前盘点 + 在非生产环境预演更新流程，因为明天 14:00 之后没有时间学新命令。

### nginx 三个 9.2 分漏洞：而真正决定你危不危险的，不是版本号，是你的配置文件里有没有那几个组合
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-20_nginx-three-critical-flaws-config-dependent/
Date: 2026-10-20
Category: 安全/运维
Source: CSO Online 报道 + NVD 三个 CVE 官方记录逐条核对
Summary: F5 为 nginx 发了三个 CVSS v4.0 9.2 的应急补丁（CVE-2026-15176 / 97205 / 93479），影响 NGINX Plus、开源版、Ingress Controller、Gateway Fabric、Instance Manager。本文的核心论点是：把这件事框架成「应急补丁」会让人做错第一件事，因为三个洞全部依赖特定配置组合才可达——15176 需要 location 同时用 alias + rewrite + 引用 $request_filename（或 access log 里用该变量）；97205 需要 AIO 与 SSI 同时启用；93479 需要 map 用正则匹配且 root 或 log_format 在引用 map 输出变量之前引用了捕获变量。所以「我危不危险」的正确问法不是「我跑哪个版本」，是「我的配置里有没有这三种组合」。文章还纠正了 CSO 的两处偏差：97205 是 use-after-free（CWE-416）而不是堆溢出（CWE-122）；三个洞的 CVSS 向量都是 AC:H（攻击复杂度高），与「应急」的印象存在张力，但两句话合起来才完整。另记录 Dickson 两句最有价值的话：「厂商网站上的修复并不能修补你的服务器」，以及「这些漏洞需要正确的配置才能咬人，而这是好消息。坏消息是很多组织可能不知道自己的 nginx 配置到底写了什么」。给出了 grep 三个组合的具体命令、ASLR 检查（randomize_va_space 应为 2，容器内也要查）、以及「worker 进程反复重启」这个共同监控信号。背景部分记录 F5 过去五年被 CISA 标记八个主动利用漏洞（四个用于勒索软件）、5 月的 NGINX Rift（CVE-2026-42945）带公开 RCE PoC，以及「攻击者也会读变更日志」这句话的含义：配置依赖不构成安全，因为攻击者会定向扫描。

### PwnEscape 的补丁已经发了，而真正的教训是：KVM 逃逸出来的地方，不是 hypervisor，是主机内核的最低层
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-20_pwnescape-kvm-escape-broader-attack-surface/
Date: 2026-10-20
Category: 安全/运维
Source: CSO Online 分析（Lucian Constantin）+ NVD + 前作技术报告
Summary: 这是对 PwnEscape（CVE-2026-99999）的第二次写作，专门写 CSO 这篇报道提供的增量，不重复技术机制。三处增量：① Edera CTO Alex Zenla 的架构论点——「当一个 guest 突破出来，它不是逃进某个被规整封装好的 hypervisor；它可能落进那个拥有主机进程、驱动和网络栈的操作系统的最低层」，因为这个区别，KVM 逃逸与「被刻意设计成极小特权层」的 hypervisor 逃逸是完全不同的安全命题；配合他的设计原则「安全架构必须假设最终会有某个东西被攻破，并确保那个攻破不会变成对主机的完全拥有」。② Januscape 对照：Januscape 影响 KVM 的内存管理代码，而 PwnEscape 的漏洞代码在通用 IPv4 网络子系统里，所以「VM 逃逸」这个分类已经不太有用了，两者的防御含义完全不同。③ AWS 声明：托管 EC2/Lambda/Fargate 不受影响，但自建 KVM + virtio-net 需要打补丁，且「只更新 guest 不能修复这个漏洞」——必须更新 host。另记录 Red Hat 把 OpenShift 容器平台组件列为受影响、Docker 与 Xen 尚未发公告（沉默≠不受影响）、以及补丁可能被回移到旧内核所以不能靠内核主版本号判断。还指出原始报告的「证据阶梯」克制在二次传播中被丢弃，失去限定条件的结论会被读成比实际更强的断言。

### Omarchy 4.5-RC1 开始支持 aarch64：而这次真正的进展不是「多了一个架构」，是三个完全不同来源的 ARM 笔记本同时跑起来了
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-20_omarchy-4-5-rc1-aarch64-snapdragon-n1x/
Date: 2026-10-20
Category: Linux/运维
Source: Phoronix 报道 + Omarchy v4.5.0-rc1 官方发布说明（GitHub Releases）+ 仓库元信息实测
Summary: Omarchy 4.5-RC1 第一次把 aarch64 变成正式支持的架构。本文的核心论点是：值得写的不是「多了个架构」，是它同时让三个完全不同来源的 ARM 生态跑起来——高通的 Snapdragon X（联想 Yoga Slim 7x 与 ThinkPad T14s，实现方式是「安装程序从 Windows 分区拉取 GPU 和 DSP 固件 + 启动时挑正确设备树」）、NVIDIA N1X（ASUS ProArt P14 与 Dell XPS 16，走 aarch64 自维护内核 + NVIDIA 开源驱动）、以及通过合并 Omarchy Mac 为 Apple Silicon 铺路（但 Phoronix 提醒「上游 Linux 对较新 M 系列仍然差得远」）。因为 ARM 笔记本的根本问题是每台机器的固件、设备树、GPU 驱动都不同，所以「支持一个架构」在实践中等于「支持一批具体型号」，而这一版做了三类。文章还指出 aarch64 只提供一个 ISO，意味着同一镜像要带多套设备树和多种 GPU 驱动并在启动时决定用哪套。x86 侧挑出三条日常改动：Limine 菜单等待从约 6 秒降到 1 秒（保留「按任意键进菜单」）、每显示器独立工作区（插上后拿回同样工作区）、通知系统重做（从一个插件 Omapager 长成内置功能）。另注意仓库已从 basecamp/omarchy 迁到 omacom/omarchy（45,355 stars / 5,608 forks，Shell，MIT），这个组织名变化意味着从「某公司的项目」变成独立项目。

### 加密 DNS 确实比 VPN 划算：但它藏住的是「你查了哪个域名」，不是「你连了哪个 IP」
URL: https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-20_encrypted-dns-providers-adguard-controld/
Date: 2026-10-20
Category: 安全/运维
Source: AdGuard DNS 隐私政策与知识库 + Control D 官方说明与隐私政策 + Windscribe 无日志档案（均一手核实）
Summary: 用户材料的核心论证成立：HTTPS 只加密内容，DNS 查询仍是明文，所以 ISP 不需要解密就能知道你访问了哪些域名；而用 VPN 解决的成本结构不对（全部流量绕一圈），加密 DNS 是精确且近零开销的解法。本文补的是边界与细节。边界：加密 DNS 藏住「你向解析器查了哪个域名」，但没藏住「你最终连了哪个 IP」（IP 头明文），也没藏住 TLS 握手里的 SNI，那一层需要 ECH，而 ECH 的前提恰恰是 DNS 必须加密。三处需要精确化的核实：① AdGuard 的「24 小时」是滚动窗口而不是「攒 24 小时后删除」，且保留目的是「识别与封锁新追踪器」，而它的私人 DNS（需注册账号）会存日志、并在你主动启用时记录「限于子网」的匿名化 IP；② AdGuard 自己在知识库里把 DNSCrypt 标注为「过时协议，支持有限」，因为它从未获得 RFC；③ Control D 的「不绑定 IP」是有条件的：必须用 Secure DNS 且关闭 Auto Authorize IPs，而用 Legacy DNS 时因 IP 耗尽必须存源 IP（IPv6 解析器不受此限制）。另记录 Windscribe 的无日志承诺被物理验证过三次（2026-02 荷兰当局从机架取走服务器，RAM-only，找到的是空的），以及 Control D 的 ctrld 就是 Windscribe DNS 功能的实现基础。
Key topics: 加密 DNS, DoH, DoT, DoQ, DNSCrypt, DNS-over-HTTPS, DNS-over-TLS, DNS-over-QUIC, HTTPS 只加密内容, ISP 监控, VPN 对比, AdGuard DNS, 24 小时滚动窗口, 私人 AdGuard DNS, 子网级匿名 IP, Control D, Auto Authorize IPs, Legacy DNS, 解析器 ID, EDNS Client Subnet, Query Name Minimisation, Full Analytics 3 天, Windscribe, RAM-only, 荷兰当局, INTERPOL, ctrld, SNI, ECH, Encrypted Client Hello, 外层 SNI, HTTPS RR, Cloudflare, Firefox, Android 私人 DNS 用 DoT

Title: 补丁还没发布，攻击就已经开始了：一个在 PHP 里躺了二十年的缺陷，让你写的 Hello World 也能被一击拿下

Date: 2026-10-21
Category: 安全/运维
Source: PingCAP Trust Hub 官方事件报告（一手，读全文）+ 攻击方 FulcrumSec 公开页面 + LavX News
Summary: PingCAP 于 2026-10-19 在 Trust Hub 发布官方安全事件报告，确认 2026-09-09 至 10-07 期间有人使用窃取的服务账号凭证访问内部系统、复制数据并获取源代码，10-07 发现当日开始停用凭证。本文把官方声明与攻击方说法并排放置，并明确标注每条来源。官方确认泄露三类客户数据：① 用户名与邮箱、组织与项目关联、SQL 编辑器文本与错误信息、组织/项目/集群标识符；② 客户联系人、合同条款、订单、定价、付款条件、计费配置；③ 一张含加密 API Key 值的表（官方测试仅一个「调查人员自己持有的」值无法直接使用，样本量为 1 且非真实客户值）。官方明确「未发现攻击者执行命令或维持持久访问」但同时自我修正「这个发现并不能消除上面描述的数据泄露」。攻击方声称 10.6 TB / 490 万文件 / 180,046 租户组织 / 20,645,574 条客户 SQL / 115,308 组明文 API Key（42,612 仍有效，与官方「加密」说法直接矛盾）。最刺眼的一句是「用提交在他们自己仓库里的凭证（GCP 服务账号密钥和一个 Azure service principal）搭起复制流，88 次连续导出，没有一次检测事件」。另记录攻击方引用的一份 2022-08 内部工单 SECURITY-22：「组织内的所有角色（包括 owner、audit admin、billing admin、member）都可以无条件地重置组织内所有集群的 root 密码」，以及工单里粘贴客户生产凭证的具体案例（含一个覆盖 258 个不属于 PingCAP 的 S3 桶的 AdministratorAccess key）。本文的判断：这次泄露的性质不是「客户业务数据被拖库」，而是「客户如何连接其业务数据的一切」被成套交付（目标清单 + 登入材料 + 攻击面信息），构成一条完整的二次攻击链。
